Asks him to let it go. A scared or tired man may take it and ease off; a proud or hot-headed one gets angrier.
Owns up to it. If he takes it he eases off, and his outfit thinks a little better of you.
$10 for his trouble - a small softening, more for a greedy man. Proud men send it back. Each one this week is worth less.
$25 to call it square. Greedy, poor or scared men may take it and ease right off; if not, the money comes back.
Tries to scare him off. Cowards back away; braver men get angrier.
Tells him you're on your way. Scares a coward; makes a braver man ready for you.
Mocks him. A proud man or a hothead takes it hard; others shrug it off.
Threatens his family. Terrifies a frightened man - and enrages a brave one.
Asks where his boss rides from. A greedy, scared or disloyal man may give the camp away.
Says his boss is selling him out. A disloyal or ambitious man may turn on him.
Gloats about the relative you killed. Pure hate - or grief, if he's scared enough.
No hard feelings. Plain men soften a little; proud men and hotheads scorn it.
Condolences for someone he lost. He eases off - a loyal man most of all.
$25 for his outfit's leader. A greedy leader takes it gladly; a proud one sends it back. Can lower your notoriety with them.
Keeps you on good terms - he'll like you a little more.
Asks what's going on round his way - fights, men with a grudge, the talk of the town.
Finds out if anyone's been asking after you in his town.
Thanks him for what he did - he'll like you more.
$2 for a drink on you - he'll like you more, unless he holds a grudge.
Asks him to wire you $10. A friend who owes you may; others won't - and it costs a little goodwill.
Asks him to watch for trouble - if he agrees, he'll wire you when a nemesis turns up near him.
Apologises - eases a grudge and some of his fear.
A friendly word - he'll like you a little more and hold a little less against you.
A proper letter - if he likes you he writes back with his own news. Write too often and he tires of it.
$5 for him - he'll like you more. A proud man may send it back.
Condolences for a friend he lost - unless he knows it was you.
Warns him to keep quiet about what he saw. He's more afraid of you and less likely to tell the law - but he'll like you less.

Get yer hands off me, ye feckin' animal.
Van der Linde's dog. I knew it.
Ye picked the wrong Irishman to grab.
Go on then. What d'ye want?
Jaysus, the smell on ye. What is it?
Ye think ye scare me? I've been beaten by better on a Sunday.
Dutch send ye? Course he did. Coward.
Ah, the famous Arthur Morgan. Dutch's errand boy.
Let go o' me collar before I bite yer hand off.
Ye'll be sorry ye ever crossed the boys, so ye will.
Well? Out with it. I haven't got all day.
Is this how Dutch's lot say hello now?
Ye've a death wish, grabbin' one of Colm's own.
Feck off and die somewhere quiet.
Ye want somethin'? Ask nice and I might laugh.
Jaysus, Mary and Joseph... don't kill me.
Easy, easy! I'm just a lad from Cork, I'm nobody!
Please, mister - I only ride with 'em for the money.
Mother of God. Alright. Alright, what d'ye want?
Don't! I've done nothin' to Dutch, I swear it!
Holy Saint Patrick... put the gun down, please.
I'm only new, mister, I don't know a thing!
Ah God, ah God, I don't want to die in this country.
I'll tell ye nothin', ye Van der Linde scum.
Colm'd have me tongue out. I'd rather it was you.
Ye can kill me. Colm'll kill ye slower.
We don't squeal. Not to Dutch's lot.
Ask yer precious Dutch. He knows all about runnin'.
I've seen Pinkertons try harder than you.
Ye'll get more out of a dead sheep.
Ye'll get the same from me as the Pinkertons get from Colm. Nothin'.
Me lips are sealed tighter than a priest's purse.
Talkin' to ye? I'd sooner drink English beer.
Ye want answers? Go to confession.
Colm's been hunted half his life. He didn't last this long with rats about.
I'll take it to me grave and spit on yers.
There's nothin' ye can do to me that Colm can't do worse.
Ask Dutch about Colm's brother. Then ask me nothin'.
I can't! Colm hangs rats from the trees, ye don't understand!
Please - he'd find out. He always finds out.
They'll string me up at Six Point if I talk. Please...
I swear on me mother, I can't say!
He'd skin me, mister, he'd skin me alive!
Please, ye don't know what he does to talkers!
I've seen what's left of the last fella who blabbed. Please.
Don't make me. Colm's got ears everywhere.
That's all ye'll get about that.
Ask me that again and ye'll be askin' a corpse.
Ye can ask the Pope. Ye'll get nothin' more.
That's the end of it, boyo.
Me mouth's shut on that, and it's stayin' shut.
Ha! Ye punch like a Protestant.
That's it? Me granny hits harder.
Is that it? Me sister's got a better right hook.
Ha! I've had worse in a Dublin pub.
Go on, ye've loosened a tooth. Proud of yerself?
Not the face, not the face!
Alright! Alright, ye made yer point!
Ye'll get that back tenfold, boyo.
Put it away, put the blade away!
Ah God, it won't stop bleedin'!
Not the knife, please, not the knife!
Aagh! Ye shot me! Ye shot me, ye bastard!
Colm'll have yer heart for that!
Ye shot me in the leg! Ye feckin' animal!
That's a bullet ye'll get back, Morgan.
I'll talk! Don't shoot me again, I'll talk!
Stop, stop! Mother of God, I'm hit!
I'll say whatever ye want! Just no more!
Is that meant to scare me?
Ha! Dutch teach ye to shoot like that?
Jaysus! That near took me ear off!
Holy God! Mind where ye point that!
Do it then. Colm'll avenge me.
I'll see ye in hell, Morgan.
Ye'll be dead in a ditch within the week.
Go on. The boys'll drink to me tonight.
Threaten all ye like. I'm Irish. We're born to suffer.
No! No, don't, please - I've a sister in Boston!
Please, I'll go back to Ireland, ye'll never see me again!
Big talk for a Van der Linde.
Colm's said worse to me over breakfast.
We'll see who's sayin' that in a month.
Keep yer dirty dollars. Colm's family.
Ye think I'd sell me own for Van der Linde money?
Shove yer money where the sun don't shine.
Colm took me in when I'd nothin'. Ye can't buy that.
Now there's a language I speak.
Ah, money. Ye should've led with that, boyo.
Jaysus, that's more than Colm pays in a month.
Now ye're talkin' sense, so ye are.
Ye think that impresses me? I've robbed better men than you of more.
Pocket change. I've drunk more than that in a night.
God bless ye... I haven't eaten in two days.
That'll put me halfway to a boat home. Alright, ask.
A few dollars won't make me a rat. But go on.
Ye didn't hear this from me.
Swear ye'll never say where ye heard it.
Here's the truth, for what it's worth.
Alright! I'll tell ye, I'll tell ye!
Don't let Colm know it was me...
I'll tell ye everythin', just put it down!
Please, it's all I know, I swear!
Ye're lettin' me walk? Ye're softer than they say.
I'll not forget this, boyo. Not sure yet which way.
Next time we meet, I'll pretend I never saw ye.
Don't expect a pint for it.
Colm'd have shot me. Strange world.
God bless ye, God bless ye, I'm gone!
Ye'll not see me again, I swear on Saint Patrick!
Thank ye, thank ye - I'm off to Boston, so I am!
